p: Hill's casual permission to Heth to 'advance and get those shoes' set in motion a battle neither Lee nor Meade had chosen to fight here.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Heth and Hill confer.”, Day 1

p: Johnson's Confederate division arrives on the Hanover Road. Positions east of Gettysburg. Faces Culp's Hill. Ewell places his corps in a line stretching from Culp's Hill to north of town.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Johnson's Confederate division arrives on the Hanover Road.”, Day 1

p: XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill. Greene's brigade on the right. Powers Hill reserve. XII Corps secures the Union right flank.

p.short: Site chronology entry “XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill.”, Day 1

p: Meade replaces Doubleday with Newton to command I Corps. II Corps (Hancock) begins arriving and extending the Union line south on Cemetery Ridge. Birney's III Corps division arrives.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Meade replaces Doubleday with Newton to command I Corps.”, Day 1

p: Both armies consolidate overnight positions. Lee reconnoiters the Union line from Seminary Ridge. Longstreet argues again for a strategic flanking movement. Lee overrules — orders Longstreet to attack the Union left. The attack is to begin as early as possible.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Both armies consolidate overnight positions.”, Day 2

p: Lee's decision to attack on July 2 rather than maneuver is the second most-debated Confederate command decision of the battle.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Both armies consolidate overnight positions.”, Day 2

p: Sickles examines his assigned position on lower Cemetery Ridge and is dissatisfied. He believes the Peach Orchard ridge is higher ground and would be better. He begins to consider an unauthorized advance.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Sickles examines his assigned position on lower Cemetery Ridge and is dissatisfied.”, Day 2

p: Longstreet's corps begins moving south for the flanking march. The march is complicated by the need to avoid Union observation from Little Round Top. Longstreet is slow and deliberate — the controversial delay begins.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Longstreet's corps begins moving south for the flanking march.”, Day 2

p: Berdan's sharpshooters (1st US Sharpshooters) sent into Pitzer's Woods by Sickles for reconnaissance. They find Wilcox's Confederate infantry. This confirms Confederate presence on Seminary Ridge south of town.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Berdan's sharpshooters (1st US Sharpshooters) sent into Pitzer's Woods by Sickles for…”, Day 2

p: Hood's division completes the flanking march and deploys south of Gettysburg. McLaws deploys north of Hood along Warfield Ridge. Alexander positions his artillery. The assault force is in position.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Hood's division completes the flanking march and deploys south of Gettysburg.”, Day 2

p: Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard — without orders, without informing Meade, without permission. Creates a salient with an exposed apex at the Orchard and a dangerously thin line stretching to Devil's Den.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard — without orders, without…”, Day 2

p: Sickles's unauthorized advance was tactically disastrous but may have drawn Confederate attention away from the Round Tops.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard — without orders, without…”, Day 2

p: Meade discovers Sickles's unauthorized advance. Furious confrontation. Meade orders Sickles back — but Confederate artillery has already opened fire and it is too late to withdraw without chaos.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Meade discovers Sickles's unauthorized advance.”, Day 2

p: LONGSTREET'S ASSAULT BEGINS. Alexander's Confederate artillery opens fire on the Peach Orchard salient — 54 guns. Hood's division steps off in Line of Battle heading northeast toward Devil's Den and the Round Tops.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Longstreet's Assault Begins”, Day 2

p: Hood severely wounded — arm permanently paralyzed by artillery fragment. Law assumes division command. Hood's request to swing around Big Round Top is denied by Longstreet.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Hood severely wounded — arm permanently paralyzed by artillery fragment.”, Day 2

p: Law's brigade (formerly Hood's) reaches Big Round Top. 15th Alabama turns left and begins assaulting the southern slope of Little Round Top. Robertson's Texas Brigade engages Ward's Union brigade at Devil's Den and the Triangular Field.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Law's brigade (formerly Hood's) reaches Big Round Top.”, Day 2
